fine_trace.note: Allocates the loader context; with WASM_ENABLE_FAST_INTERP, preserved_local_offset is initialized to INT16_MAX for the first traverse.
The compiled-code buffer size is tracked only during the first pass via increase_compiled_code_space.
Each opcode starts by emitting its label; disable_emit is reset to false at the top of the loop.
For I32_CONST, the label is removed and the const pool is consulted; if the constant is already pooled, disable_emit stays true and no code is emitted.
In the first pass, when the const pool is full, the constant is NOT added and offset 0 is returned, causing the const instruction to be emitted inline.

fine_trace.code: if (operand_offset == 0) { disable_emit = false; emit_label(WASM_OP_I32_CONST); emit_uint32(loader_ctx, i32_const); }
fine_trace.note: When the pool is full, the label and 4-byte constant are emitted inline, increasing code_compiled_size in the first pass.
After the first pass, re_scan is triggered; wasm_loader_ctx_reinit allocates code_compiled_peak_size bytes for p_code_compiled.
The compiled-code buffer is allocated with the peak size recorded during the first pass; writes in the second pass go directly to this buffer without bounds checks.

fine_trace.code: i32_const = bsearch(&key, ctx->i32_consts, ctx->i32_const_num, sizeof(int32), cmp_i32_const); if (!i32_const) { *offset = 0; return true; }
fine_trace.note: In the second pass, constants that were not added to the pool in the first pass (because the pool was full) are not found, so offset 0 is returned and the const instruction is emitted inline again.
In the second pass, the inline const emission writes to p_code_compiled; if the total emitted bytes exceed code_compiled_peak_size, this is a heap-buffer-overflow WRITE.
The 4-byte write advances p_code_compiled past the allocated buffer end, causing the heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 reported by ASan.
